PullRequest.Title: welcome: Restore GitHub sign-in banner and enable by default

Experiment: microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#9359
Originally added in #336437 and removed in #342422.

The experiment for the "Sign in to GitHub" banner on the classic Welcome page is shipping (ExP is rolling the treatment to 100% on Stable 1.139+). This PR restores the feature and turns it on by default in code.

### Changes

1. **Revert #342422** (`git revert -m 1 c879d0061f4841e644f108dd1c0333fda24df5fa`). The revert applied cleanly. No later commits on `main` touched the affected files, and the result is identical to the tree before #342422. This restores:
   - `ChatConfiguration.WelcomePageSignInEnabled` and the `chat.welcomePage.signIn.enabled` registration (`experiment: { mode: 'auto' }`)
   - the sign-in branch in `agentSessionsBanner.ts`
   - passing `IDefaultAccountService` to the banner from `gettingStarted.ts`
   - the banner unit tests

   The 1-line change that #336437 made to `agentSessionsWelcome.ts` (passing `configurationService`) is still on `main`, because #342422 didn't remove it. That page does not pass the default-account service, so it never offers sign-in.
2. **Enable by default.** The `chat.welcomePage.signIn.enabled` default changes from `false` to `true`. The setting and `experiment: { mode: 'auto' }` remain, so ExP assignments and explicit user settings can still turn it off. The banner now treats an unset value as enabled (`!== false` instead of `=== true`), so its fallback matches the registered default. Tests now use the unset/default configuration. A resolved signed-out account sees "Sign in to GitHub" by default, and an explicit `false` keeps "Try out the new Agents window".

### Behavior

- If the default account has resolved as signed out, the button shows "Sign in to GitHub" (GitHub icon) and starts the default-account sign-in.
- Signed-in users, and users whose account has not resolved yet, see "Try out the new Agents window".
- After sign-in, the same button switches back to "Try out the new Agents window".

### Timing

This should merge before `release/1.143` branches so that 1.143+ keeps the behavior without depending on the ExP assignment.

### Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client` (repo equivalent of `compile-check-ts-native`, which does not exist in this repo): passed
- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only`: passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentSessionsBanner.test.ts --grep "AgentsBanner"`: passed (20 passing)
- `npm run eslint -- <5 changed files>`: passed (0 problems)
- `node build/hygiene.ts <5 changed files>`: passed (the pre-commit hygiene hook also passed)

Not run: manual testing in a running build, and the full unit/integration suites.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or rebuild the classic Welcome page and construct the Agents banner
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Welcome-page DOM construction completes synchronously; the new getDefaultAccount() promise is not awaited by buildCategoriesSlide, so account resolution and the subsequent constant-time label/icon update are off the page-render critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the default authentication provider, read provider sessions, and refresh cache-controlled account entitlement/policy data.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shared provider initialization/refresh per workbench startup, already scheduled by DefaultAccountProviderContribution at WorkbenchPhase.BlockStartup. Any number of banner calls only wait on the same init barrier and add zero refreshes; successful entitlement/policy reads are cache-controlled, while provider session reads have bounded retries on failure.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The default-account provider and its startup refresh already ran at BlockStartup even when the Welcome banner did not call getDefaultAccount().
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The banner waits only to change its action after resolution; it does not block Welcome-page construction or interaction.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One banner per GettingStartedPage; rebuild frequency is driven by input or walkthrough changes, with the prior banner's DisposableStore cleared before replacement.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each live Welcome page has one pending waiter on the shared initialization barrier. Rebuilds dispose prior listeners; no account refresh is launched by the banner and no boundary fan-out occurs.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The banner reads the service's resolved in-memory account. Cold startup waits on the existing shared initialization; warm/rebuilt banners resolve immediately. Provider entitlement/policy caches and throttling remain unchanged, and the banner introduces no cache key or negative-cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: createAgentsBanner calls getDefaultAccount(), whose implementation only waits on initBarrier; provider refresh is independently registered at BlockStartup, and prior banner listeners are cleared on rebuild.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact startup account-refresh duration varies by authentication provider and network state, but that work is pre-existing and off the Welcome render critical path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds bounded DOM/listener work and a waiter on pre-existing shared initialization, not new IPC/network operations or blocking startup work.

Scenarios.Scenario: React to default-account or experiment-setting changes while the Welcome page is open
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The event handler synchronously computes one boolean and updates one button title, one text node, and two CSS classes.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost is O(1) per account/configuration event and does not scale with walkthrough, recent-item, or account collection size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Events are delivered synchronously to one listener per live banner; old listeners are disposed when the categories slide rebuilds or the editor is disposed.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Reads currentDefaultAccount and configuration in memory; no cache miss, filesystem, IPC, or network operation is triggered.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed handlers directly perform only in-memory reads and constant-size DOM mutations, with explicit DisposableStore ownership.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Event frequency is environment-dependent, but account and targeted configuration changes are infrequent and each update is fixed-size.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; there is no unbounded retention, repeated collection work, layout read/write cycle, or expensive boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Click the restored Sign in to GitHub action
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After account initialization is resolved, the click invokes defaultAccountService.signIn(); authentication provider activation/session creation must complete for sign-in to finish, but this is the requested interaction rather than page startup/render work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create an authentication session through the configured default authentication provider and then reconcile the default account.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One authentication session creation per explicit sign-in click; no loop or collection fan-out is added.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The banner click executed the Agents-window command instead of starting authentication.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The boundary is on the explicit sign-in interaction path and determines completion of authentication, but the promise is not awaited by the UI event handler and does not block rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Emit the existing agentsBanner.clicked telemetry event with the new signIn action value.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One telemetry emission per explicit click, matching the pre-diff click telemetry cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same click emitted agentsBanner.clicked with action openAgentsWindow.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Telemetry emission is not awaited and is off the authentication completion path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Scales only with explicit user clicks, not with account/session collection size or Welcome-page rebuilds.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One call per ordinary user click. The diff adds no loop, fan-out, background scheduling, or automatic retry; repository code does not establish a realistic high-cardinality click burst that would justify a concurrency finding.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The action is offered only after shared initial account resolution confirms a signed-out state. Authentication itself is intentionally not cached as a completed sign-in operation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the single authentication boundary and its call path; low for any material burst hypothesis, so no finding is warranted.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider latency varies and rapid repeated clicks are theoretically possible, but there is no evidenced realistic scaling trigger or demonstrated material performance impact beyond the intended authentication operation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The new boundary is the intentional, user-triggered feature behavior with bounded cardinality.

Scenarios.Scenario: Register the Welcome-page sign-in configuration and default it on
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Configuration metadata is registered during chat contribution loading; no new per-render or per-event computation is introduced.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed one-setting metadata cost independent of workspace size or user data.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single configuration registration; experiment assignment infrastructure remains shared and unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Configuration and experiment assignment use existing shared services; the diff adds no independent fetch or cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from the changed registration hunk and surrounding configuration pattern.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Negligible fixed metadata allocation; no scaling or external boundary was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; this is fixed-size startup metadata and does not introduce a new expensive boundary.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all five changed files and all diff pages. Traced Welcome construction/rebuild, account/configuration events, explicit sign-in, service initialization, authentication boundaries, cache behavior, concurrency, and disposal. No actionable diff-introduced performance regression or qualifying regression fix was found.
